section_desc: This Act applies to any person who is a Hindu by religion in any of its forms or developments, including a Virashaiva, a Lingayat or a follower of the Brahmo, Prarthana or Arya Samaj; to any person who is a Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh by religion; to any other person domiciled in the territories to which this Act extends who is not a Muslim, Christian, Parsi or Jew by religion. The expression 'Hindu' shall be construed accordingly.

A Hindu marriage may be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies of either party thereto. Where such rites and ceremonies include the Saptapadi (taking of seven steps by the bridegroom and the bride jointly before the sacred fire), the marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken.

For the purpose of facilitating the proof of Hindu marriages, the State Government may make rules providing that the parties to any such marriage may have the particulars relating to their marriage entered in such manner and subject to such conditions as may be prescribed in a Hindu Marriage Register kept for the purpose. Registration is voluntary under HMA but may be made compulsory by State Government rules.

When either the husband or the wife has, without reasonable excuse, withdrawn from the society of the other, the aggrieved party may apply by petition to the district court for restitution of conjugal rights and the court, on being satisfied of the truth of the statements made in such petition and that there is no legal ground why the application should not be granted, may decree restitution of conjugal rights accordingly.

Either party to a marriage, whether solemnized before or after the commencement of this Act, may present a petition praying for a decree for judicial separation on any of the grounds specified in sub-section (1) of section 13, and in the case of a wife also on any of the grounds specified in sub-section (2) thereof, as grounds for divorce.

Any marriage solemnized after the commencement of this Act shall be null and void and may, on a petition presented by either party thereto against the other party, be so declared by a decree of nullity if it contravenes any one of the conditions specified in clauses (i), (iv) and (v) of section 5 — i.e., if either party has a spouse living, or the parties are within prohibited degrees or sapinda relationship.

Any marriage solemnized, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be voidable and may be annulled by a decree of nullity on any of the following grounds: the marriage has not been consummated owing to the impotence of the respondent; the marriage is in contravention of the condition specified in clause (ii) of section 5 (unsoundness of mind); the consent of the petitioner or the guardian was obtained by force or fraud; the respondent was at the time of marriage pregnant by some other person.

section_title: No petition for divorce to be presented within one year of marriage
section_desc: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, it shall not be competent for any court to entertain any petition for dissolution of a marriage by a decree of divorce, unless at the date of the presentation of the petition one year has elapsed since the date of the marriage. Provided that the court may, upon application made to it in accordance with such rules as may be made by the High Court in that behalf, allow a petition to be presented before one year has elapsed on the ground that the case is one of exceptional hardship to the petitioner or of exceptional depravity on the part of the respondent.

section_title: Divorced persons when may marry again
section_desc: When a marriage has been dissolved by a decree of divorce and either there is no right of appeal against the decree or, if there is such a right of appeal, the time for appealing has expired without an appeal having been presented, or an appeal has been presented but has been dismissed, it shall be lawful for either party to the marriage to marry again.

section_title: Legitimacy of children of void and voidable marriages
section_desc: Notwithstanding that a marriage is null and void under section 11, any child of such marriage who would have been legitimate if the marriage had been valid, shall be legitimate, whether or not a decree of nullity is granted in respect of that marriage under this Act and whether or not the marriage is held to be void otherwise than on a petition under this Act.

Any marriage between two Hindus solemnized after the commencement of this Act is void if at the date of such marriage either party had a husband or wife living; and the provisions of sections 494 and 495 of the Indian Penal Code (corresponding sections 59 and 60 of BNS) shall apply accordingly.

section_title: Punishment for contravention of certain other conditions for a Hindu marriage
section_desc: Every person who procures a marriage of himself or herself to be solemnized under this Act in contravention of the conditions specified in clauses (iii), (iv) and (v) of section 5 shall be punishable: in the case of a contravention of clause (iii) — simple imprisonment for up to fifteen days, or fine up to one thousand rupees; in the case of a contravention of clauses (iv) and (v) — simple imprisonment for up to one month, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.

section_title: Court to which petition shall be presented
section_desc: Every petition under this Act shall be presented to the district court within the local limits of whose ordinary original civil jurisdiction the marriage was solemnized, or the respondent, at the time of the presentation of the petition, resides, or the parties to the marriage last resided together, or in the case the petitioner is residing out of India, where the petitioner resides.

section_title: Power to transfer petitions in certain cases
section_desc: Where a petition under this Act has been presented to a district court and another petition from the other spouse is pending in a different district court, the Supreme Court or High Court may, on the application of one of the parties or on its own motion, transfer either petition to the other court. The court to which the petition is transferred shall then proceed to try both petitions together.

In any proceeding under this Act, whether defended or not, if the court is satisfied that the statements made in the petition are true, and if the court is not satisfied that the petitioner is in any way taking advantage of his or her own wrong or disability, and that there has not been any unnecessary or improper delay in instituting the proceeding, and that no other legal ground exists for refusing the reliefs prayed for, then the court shall proceed to pass a decree.

section_title: Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings
section_desc: Where in any proceeding under this Act it appears to the court that either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, has no independent income sufficient for her or his support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may, on the application of the wife or the husband, order the respondent to pay to the petitioner the expenses of the proceeding, and monthly during the proceeding such sum as, having regard to the petitioner's own income and the income of the respondent, it may seem to the court to be reasonable.

Any court exercising jurisdiction under this Act may, at the time of passing any decree or at any time subsequent thereto, on application made to it for the purpose by either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, order that the respondent shall pay to the applicant for her or his maintenance and support such gross sum or such monthly or periodical sum for a term not exceeding the life of the applicant as, having regard to the respondent's own income and other property, if any, the income and other property of the applicant and the conduct of the parties and other circumstances of the case, it may seem to the court to be just.

In any proceeding under this Act, the court may, from time to time, pass such interim orders and make such provisions in the decree as it may deem just and proper with respect to the custody, maintenance and education of minor children, consistently with their wishes, wherever possible, and may, after the decree, upon application by petition for the purpose, make, revoke, suspend or vary from time to time, all such orders and provisions with respect to the custody, maintenance and education of such children.

In any proceeding under this Act, the court may make such provisions in the decree as it deems just and proper with respect to any property presented, at or about the time of marriage, which may belong jointly to both the husband and the wife. Stridhan and matrimonial gifts may be included.

All decrees made by the court in any proceeding under this Act shall, subject to the provisions of sub-section (3), be appealable as decrees of the court made in the exercise of its original civil jurisdiction and every such appeal shall lie to the court to which appeals ordinarily lie from the decisions of the court making the decree. Every order made by the court in any proceeding under this Act under section 25 or section 26 shall, subject to the provisions of sub-section (3), be appealable.

In this Act: 'agnate' means a person related by blood or adoption wholly through males; 'cognate' means a person related by blood or adoption, but not wholly through males; 'full blood' — two persons are said to be related to each other by full blood when they are descended from a common ancestor by the same wife; 'half blood' — two persons are related by half blood when descended from a common ancestor but by different wives; 'intestate' — a person is deemed to die intestate in respect of all property of which he has not made a testamentary disposition.

Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act, any text, rule or interpretation of Hindu law or any custom or usage as part of that law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect with respect to any matter for which provision is made in this Act. Nothing contained in this Act shall be deemed to affect the provisions of any special enactment now in force regulating or imposing restrictions upon the succession to, or alienation of, any property.

section_title: Order of succession among heirs in Schedule
section_desc: The order of succession among the heirs referred to in section 8 shall be, and is hereby determined, in accordance with the rules of preference among heirs enumerated in the various classes listed in the Schedule. Agnates who are nearer in degree shall be preferred to those who are more remote. Between agnates of equal degree, the son is preferred to the father, and the father to the grandfather.

For the purposes of determining the order of succession among agnates or cognates, relationship shall be reckoned from the intestate to the claimant in the following manner: the intestate is the starting point and each generation including that of the claimant is a degree. Two cognates are said to be of equal degree if the total number of degrees is equal, each degree counting a generation.

section_title: Order of succession and manner of division among heirs of a female Hindu
section_desc: The order of succession among the heirs specified in sub-section (1) of section 15 shall be, and is hereby determined, in accordance with the following rules: (1) among the heirs referred to in clauses (a) and (b) of sub-section (1), those in clause (a) shall be preferred to those in clause (b); (2) among heirs referred to in clause (c) and clause (d), those in clause (c) shall be preferred; (3) the property of a female Hindu who dies without leaving any issue shall devolve, in the absence of mother and father, upon the husband's heirs and in their absence upon her father's heirs.

The provisions of sections 8 to 16 shall not apply to the property of a male Hindu who dies after the commencement of the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005. The 2005 Amendment granted daughters equal rights as sons in ancestral property, making daughters coparceners by birth in a Joint Hindu Family governed by Mitakshara law.

section_title: Full blood preferred to half blood
section_desc: Heirs related to an intestate by full blood shall be preferred to heirs related by half blood, if the nature of the relationship is the same in every other respect. The principle that closer relationship through the same mother should be preferred over relationship through different mothers when degree and type of relationship are otherwise equal.

section_title: Mode of succession of two or more heirs
section_desc: If two or more heirs succeed together to the property of an intestate, they shall take the property per capita and not per stirpes; and each of them shall have equal shares. But the share of the heirs in the second generation who succeed to the share of a pre-deceased person shall be equal.

A child who was in the womb at the time of the death of an intestate and who is subsequently born alive shall have the same right to inherit to the intestate as if he or she had been born before the death of the intestate, and the inheritance shall be deemed to vest in the child as from the date of the death of the intestate.

section_title: Presumption in cases of simultaneous deaths
section_desc: Where two persons have died in circumstances rendering it uncertain whether either of them, and if so which, survived the other, then, for all purposes affecting succession to property, it shall be presumed, until the contrary is proved, that the younger survived the elder.

section_title: Preferential right to acquire property in certain cases
section_desc: Where, after the commencement of this Act, an interest in any immovable property of an intestate, or in any business carried on by him or her, whether solely or in conjunction with others, devolves under this Act upon two or more heirs, and any one of such heirs proposes to transfer his or her interest in the property or business, the other heirs shall have a preferential right to acquire the interest proposed to be transferred.

Where a Hindu intestate has left surviving him or her both male and female heirs specified in class I of the Schedule and his or her property includes a dwelling house wholly occupied by members of his or her family, then, notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, the right of any such female heir to claim partition of the dwelling house shall not arise until the male heirs choose to divide their respective shares therein or until the property ceases to be a dwelling house of the family. This section omitted by 2005 amendment giving equal rights to daughters.

section_title: Certain widows remarrying may not inherit as widows
section_desc: Any heir who is related to an intestate as the widow of a pre-deceased son, the widow of a pre-deceased son's son, or the widow of a brother shall not be entitled to succeed to the property of the intestate as such widow, if on the date the succession opens she has remarried.

A person who commits murder or abets the commission of murder shall be disqualified from inheriting the property of the person murdered or any other property in furtherance of the succession to which he or she committed or abetted the commission of the murder.

Where, before or after the commencement of this Act, a Hindu has ceased or ceases to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion, children born to him or her after such conversion and their descendants shall be disqualified from inheriting the property of any of their Hindu relatives, unless such children or descendants are Hindus at the time when the succession opens.
If any person is disqualified from inheriting any property under this Act, it shall devolve as if such person had died before the intestate.

If an intestate has left no heir qualified to succeed to his or her property in accordance with the provisions of this Act, such property shall devolve on the government; and the government shall take the property subject to all the obligations and liabilities to which an heir would have been subject.

Any Hindu may dispose of by will or other testamentary disposition any property, which is capable of being so disposed of by him, in accordance with the provisions of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, or any other enactment for the time being in force and applicable to Hindus. A Hindu male can also bequeath his undivided Mitakshara interest in coparcenary property by will — this was not possible before the HSA.

section_title: Power of court to make order as to guardianship
section_desc: Where the court is satisfied that it is for the welfare of a minor that an order should be made appointing a guardian of his person or property, or both, or declaring a person to be such a guardian, the court may make an order accordingly. In appointing or declaring a guardian, the court shall be guided by what appears in the circumstances to be for the welfare of the minor.

section_title: Matters to be considered by the court in appointing guardian
section_desc: In appointing or declaring the guardian of a minor, the court shall, subject to the provisions of this section, be guided by what appears in the circumstances to be for the welfare of the minor. In considering what will be for the welfare of the minor, the court shall have regard to the age, sex and religion of the minor, the character and capacity of the proposed guardian and his nearness of kin to the minor, the wishes, if any, of a deceased parent, and any existing or previous relations of the proposed guardian with the minor or his property.

section_title: Title of guardian appointed or declared by court to act
section_desc: A person appointed or declared by the court to be guardian of the person of a minor is entitled to the custody of the minor. When a minor has left or been removed from the custody of a guardian of his person, the court making the order may cause the minor to be produced and to be delivered into the custody of the guardian.

section_title: Duty of guardian to deal with minor's property as prudent man
section_desc: A guardian of the property of a ward is bound to deal therewith as carefully as a man of ordinary prudence would deal with it if it were his own; and, subject to the provisions of this Act, he may do all acts which are reasonable and proper for the realisation, protection or benefit of the property.

The court may, on the application of any person interested, or of its own accord, remove from his wardship a guardian appointed or declared by the court if: the guardian has been found guilty of contumacious disregard of the orders of the court; the guardian has been found guilty of neglect of his duties; the guardian has been declared insolvent; the guardian has ceased to reside in India; the ward has been removed from the jurisdiction of the court.
chapter_title: Powers of Court with Respect to Guardians

section_title: Application of Personal Law to Muslims — extended scope
section_desc: Notwithstanding any custom or usage to the contrary, in all questions regarding intestate succession, special property of females, marriage, dissolution of marriage including talaq, ila, zihar, lian, khul and mubaraat, maintenance, dower, guardianship, gifts, trusts and trust properties, and wakfs, the rule of decision in cases where the parties are Muslims shall be Muslim Personal Law (Shariat). Talaq-e-biddat (triple talaq) declared unconstitutional by Supreme Court in Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017) and criminalized by Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.

act: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019
section_title: Triple talaq to be void and illegal
section_desc: Any pronouncement of talaq by a Muslim husband upon his wife, by words, either spoken or written or in electronic form or in any other manner whatsoever, shall be void and illegal. Triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) means talaq which is irrevocable as defined under Muslim Personal Law. The Act makes instant triple talaq a criminal offence punishable with imprisonment up to three years and fine.

act: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019
section_desc: Any Muslim husband who pronounces talaq referred to in section 3 upon his wife shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine. The offence is cognizable, non-bailable, and compoundable only if the wife so desires. Only the wife or her blood relatives may lodge an FIR.

act: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019
section_title: Allowance to wife and dependent children
section_desc: Without prejudice to her right to receive a mehr or dower under Muslim Personal Law, a married Muslim woman upon whom talaq is pronounced shall be entitled to receive from her husband such amount of allowance as determined by the magistrate and to retain the custody of her minor children as may be determined by the Magistrate having jurisdiction.

act: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986
section_desc: If a Magistrate is satisfied that a divorced woman has not been paid or is not being paid the maintenance payable under sub-section (1) of section 3, he may, by order, direct her former husband to pay to her such reasonable and fair maintenance as he may determine; the order may be enforced in the same manner as prescribed for maintenance under the Code of Criminal Procedure.

act: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986
section_title: Option to be governed by provisions of sections 125 to 128 of Code
section_desc: If, on the date of the first hearing of the application under sub-section (2) of section 3, a divorced woman and her former husband declare, by affidavit or any other declaration in writing in such form as may be prescribed, either jointly or separately, that they would prefer to be governed by the provisions of sections 125 to 128 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, and file such affidavit or declaration in the court, the Magistrate shall dispose of such application accordingly.

In this Act: 'Parsi' means a Parsi Zoroastrian; 'Parsi marriage' means a marriage contracted under the provisions of this Act between Parsis, both of whom profess the Zoroastrian religion; 'priest' means an ordained Zoroastrian priest who has duly performed the Navar ceremony; 'Parsi matrimonial court' means the special court established for hearing matrimonial cases between Parsis.

No Parsi shall contract any marriage under this Act or any other law in the lifetime of his or her husband or wife. A marriage under this Act shall not be valid unless it is solemnized according to the Ashirvad ceremony; it is performed in the presence of a priest and two Parsi witnesses; and both parties have completed the age of marriage (male: 21, female: 18). Marriages between close relations are prohibited.

section_title: Application of certain provisions to Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs and Jains
section_desc: The provisions of this Part relating to wills and codicils shall apply to wills made by any Hindu, Buddhist, Sikh or Jain on or after the first day of January 1927 except where such Hindu, Buddhist, Sikh or Jain is governed by customary law in respect of wills. The provisions regarding execution, attestation, revocation and revival of wills in this Act are applicable.

Every testator, not being a soldier employed in an expedition or engaged in actual warfare, or an airman so employed or engaged, or a mariner at sea, shall execute his will according to the following rules: the testator shall sign or shall affix his mark to the will, or it shall be signed by some other person in his presence and by his direction; the signature shall be made or acknowledged by the testator in the presence of two or more witnesses present at the same time; each witness shall sign the will in the presence of the testator, but no particular form of attestation shall be necessary.

section_title: Revocation of will by testator's marriage
section_desc: Every will shall be revoked by the marriage of the maker, except a will made in exercise of a power of appointment, when the property over which the power of appointment is exercised would not, in default of such appointment, pass to the executor or administrator or next of kin of the testator. This rule does not apply to Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs and Jains.

Probate of a will shall be granted only to an executor appointed by the will. Probate cannot be granted to a minor or to a person of unsound mind or to a body corporate. Probate shall be conclusive evidence of the due execution of the will. No action as executor can be taken by any person before probate is granted.

section_title: Intestate succession among Parsis — general rules
section_desc: In the case of a Parsi dying intestate, the rules of succession in sections 371 to 379 shall apply. The property of an intestate shall devolve on his widow, widower, and lineal descendants and not on a collateral. Where a Parsi dies without leaving any lineal descendants, his property shall devolve on his father and mother, and in equal shares. The Parsi rules of intestate succession treat male and female equally in most cases.

Every intestate's property shall be distributed among his lineal descendants, if any. If there are no lineal descendants, the property shall go to the husband or widow. Property shall go to the kindred of the intestate if there are no descendants, husband or widow. The Act provides detailed rules for division among children, grandchildren, and other relatives. The key principle is equal division per capita among persons of the same degree.
